title: Trump fights to protect agenda as America heads to polls on Election Day
content: Election Day has arrived, placing President Trump’s political capital on the line as Democrats anticipate a blue wave and Republicans work to protect congressional majorities. Trump has campaigned nationwide, holding 28 in‑person rallies and telerallies, stopping in Ohio, Texas, and other states.
summary: Election Day is here, with President Trump’s political capital on the line as Democrats eye a potential blue wave and Republicans scramble to defend their congressional majorities. Trump has campaigned across the country in recent months, holding 28 in‑person rallies and a series of telerallies, with stops in states including Ohio and Texas.

title: Ken Burns: ‘Something more fundamental at stake’ with this election
content: Filmmaker and historian Ken Burns warned on Tuesday that the U.S. faces its fourth great national crisis, stating that midterm election stakes extend beyond political differences to democracy’s survival. In a New York Times opinion piece published on Election Day, Burns accused the Trump administration of fueling misinformation.

title: Sen. Susan Collins' Maine office vandalized for second time
content: A federal constituent service office for Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) was vandalized overnight, marking the second incident in two months as the incumbent concludes a tight election race. Photos obtained by NewsNation reveal that red paint was used to write “blood on her hands” and was also splashed on the location.
summary: A federal constituent service office of Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) was vandalized overnight for the second time in two months. Photos show red paint was used to write "blood on her hands" and splash the office.

title: Election expert confident in voting process, worried about post-election events
content: Election experts express confidence in the voting process for the upcoming midterms, noting that millions of Americans have already cast their ballots. Their primary concern lies not in the act of voting itself, but in the events that will unfold after the polls close.
summary: Millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms. Election experts are more concerned about what happens after the polls close than about the voting process itself.

title: Judge considers motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's case
content: A Massachusetts judge is currently considering a motion to dismiss the case of Lindsay Clancy, who faces charges for the murder of her three children. The legal proceedings are at a stage where the court is evaluating whether to proceed with the prosecution or drop the charges entirely.
summary: A Massachusetts judge is weighing a motion to dismiss the case of Lindsay Clancy, who was charged with murdering her three children. Here's what could come next in the case.

content: Swing Shift voters, who all previously supported President Trump, are rating his presidency and determining their choices for upcoming elections where he is not a candidate. This final check-in occurs ahead of Election Day.

title: Reform UK councillor charged with rape and sexual assault
content: The leader of Reform UK in Hampshire has been charged with 35 offences against four victims over a 13-year period. The charges include 12 counts of rape, along with other sexual assault allegations.
summary: The leader of Reform UK in Hampshire has been charged with 35 offences against four victims over a 13-year period, including 12 counts of rape.
author: BBC Politics

title: New Garden Climate Assessment Tool Predicts Plant Response to Future Climate
content: The Garden Climate Assessment Tool enables users to predict how plants will respond to projected climate conditions in specific locations. This resource aims to assist gardeners in shifting away from water-intensive English classics toward drought-resistant species. Prof Sam Brockington, a curator at Cambridge University Botanic Garden, explained that while the 20th century allowed for confident cultivation based on established traditions, current climate scenarios lack the historical understanding necessary for reliable planting decisions.
summary: The Garden Climate Assessment Tool allows users to predict how plants will respond to projected climate conditions in specific locations. Prof Sam Brockington of Cambridge University Botanic Garden states that this tool is needed because current climate scenarios lack established growing traditions.
author: Guardian Environment

title: GB's worst bluetongue season called major animal welfare crisis
content:
The British Veterinary Association president informed Members of Parliament that Great Britain is experiencing its worst-ever bluetongue season, describing the situation as a major animal welfare crisis. This unprecedented surge in cases is placing farmers under severe pressure and emotional stress.

Bluetongue is a viral disease affecting sheep, cattle, and goats. The infection can result in fever, lesions, stillbirths, and death, with symptoms including a blue tongue that may protrude from the mouth.
summary: The British Veterinary Association president told MPs that the record bluetongue season is a major animal welfare crisis. The surge in cases is placing farmers under severe emotional stress.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Ohio stops issuing permits for ruffed grouse hunting due to falling numbers
content: No open permits to hunt ruffed grouse have been issued in Ohio, marking the first time since 1937 that this has occurred due to declining bird populations. Consequently, the annual November tradition of hundreds of hunters targeting the species in four designated southern Ohio wilderness areas will not take place this year.
summary: Ohio has not issued any open permits to hunt ruffed grouse for the first time since 1937. Hundreds of hunters normally hunt the ruffed grouse each November in four designated wilderness areas in southern Ohio, but this year they did not.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Tallinn University research aims to replace biopsies with blood tests
content: Doctors currently rely on tissue biopsies to diagnose conditions inside tumors or other organs. Biomedical scientist Danilo Mladenović is researching a blood test that could deliver the same diagnostic information. The study at Tallinn University may enable earlier disease detection and treatment monitoring without repeated tissue sampling.
summary: Doctors often take tissue samples to understand tumors or other affected organs. Biomedical scientist Danilo Mladenović is researching at Tallinn University to obtain the same information from blood samples, which could let doctors detect diseases earlier and monitor treatment effectiveness without repeated tissue sampling.
author: Medical Xpress

title: RA patients choosing own treatment report higher satisfaction and fewer adverse events
content: A study published online on Oct. 27 in RMD Open found that rheumatoid arthritis patients who selected their own treatment reported higher treatment satisfaction, greater retention of therapy, and fewer adverse events compared with patients who did not choose their treatment.
summary: A study published online Oct. 27 in RMD Open found that rheumatoid arthritis patients who choose their own treatment have higher treatment satisfaction. The same patients also showed better treatment retention and reported fewer adverse events.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Rx Kids Launch Cut Flint Newborn Deaths by 50%
content: A new study published in JAMA Pediatrics reports that neonatal mortality in Flint decreased by 50% after the launch of Rx Kids. The research also indicates that early neonatal mortality, defined as infant death within the first seven days of life, fell by 74% following the program's introduction.
summary: Study: Rx Kids Launch Cut Flint Newborn Deaths by 50%.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Yale researchers identify new genetic risk factors for pigmentary glaucoma
content: Yale School of Medicine researchers have identified new genetic risk factors linked to a specific subtype of glaucoma. These findings point to a novel mechanism that may play a role in the disease’s onset.
summary: Yale School of Medicine researchers have discovered new genetic risk factors associated with a subtype of glaucoma. These findings highlight a novel mechanism that may contribute to the onset of the disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ultrathin OCT endoscope developed for retinal surgery imaging
content:
Physicists from the Applied Optics Group at the University of Kent, in collaboration with partners from King's College London and Moorfields Eye Hospital, have developed a new ultrathin, forward-viewing endoscope. This device is designed to capture optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of tissue located up to approximately 1 mm beneath its surface.

The initial prototype features a diameter of just 0.31 mm, a size that makes it suitable for potential use during retinal surgery.
summary: A team from the University of Kent, King's College London, and Moorfields Eye Hospital developed an ultrathin forward-viewing endoscope that captures OCT images up to 1 mm beneath tissue. The initial prototype has a diameter of 0.31 mm, making it small enough for potential use in retinal surgery.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds Israel's warning labels easier to understand than Nutri-Score
content: A new German–Israeli eye-tracking study indicates that the design and familiarity of front-of-package nutrition labels influence consumer attention and interpretation. Participants in both countries reported that Israel’s warning-label system was easier to understand and more helpful for making healthy choices compared to the Nutri-Score. This research provides timely insights as Europe and the United States evaluate how nutrition information should be displayed on packaged foods.
summary: A German–Israeli eye-tracking study found that label design and familiarity influence how consumers interpret food products. Participants in both countries considered Israel's warning-label system easier to understand and more helpful for healthy choices than Nutri-Score.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Possible Chemical Explanation for Giving Up on Tough Tasks
content: A recent discussion highlights a common experience: when we tackle mentally demanding tasks, we eventually hit a wall or feel completely drained. Even when the payoff of finishing is clear, many of us simply stop. The exact cause of this phenomenon has long remained a mystery. While tiredness or a lack of motivation are obvious explanations, the underlying biological drivers of this disengagement are still unknown.
summary: When we engage our brains in a mentally taxing task, we eventually stop despite obvious rewards. The reason for this disengagement remains a mystery, with tiredness or lack of motivation considered but no biological explanation yet identified.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Pfizer raises outlook, appoints veteran Cecile Guegan as CFO
content: Pfizer has raised its full‑year outlook, citing growth from newer products. The company also announced that Cecile Guegan, who has held various leadership roles at Pfizer for the past 20 years, has stepped into the chief financial officer position this month.
summary: Pfizer raised its full-year outlook as newer products grow. The company stepped in Cecile Guegan as its new CFO, a veteran who has held various leadership roles for 20 years.
author: CNBC Business

title: Eau Claire artisan shop Tangled Up in Hue to close after 18 years
content: Affordability and small businesses’ economic woes feature heavily in the House race for Wisconsin’s third district After 18 years in business, Erin Klaus is closing her storefront, a handmade artisan market in downtown Eau Claire, Wisconsin, at the end of the year. She opened Tangled Up in Hue amid a recession, during a time when downtown was “kind of a ghost town”, weathering construction and the pandemic. But the current economic crisis proved too much. She’s seen a downward trend in sales for two years, and was dipping into her own pocket from her other job, as the executive director of business non-profit Downtown Eau Claire Inc, to pay staff.
summary: Eau Claire artisan shop Tangled Up in Hue to close after 18 years.
author: Guardian Business

title: Iridium catalyst designed to activate chemotherapy drug at tumor cells
content:
Conventional chemotherapy often harms healthy tissue, producing side effects such as hair loss and nausea.  

A research team led by Dr. Thomas Ward from the Department of Chemistry and the Swiss Nanoscience Institute (SNI) at the University of Basel is developing a new strategy. The approach uses artificial metal compounds as catalysts that bind specifically to tumor cells and then convert prodrugs into the active chemotherapy agent directly at the tumor site.
summary: Dr. Thomas Ward's team from the Department of Chemistry and the Swiss Nanoscience Institute at the University of Basel is developing artificial metal catalysts that bind specifically to tumor cells. The iridium catalyst they are testing converts prodrugs into the active chemotherapy ingredient directly at the tumor site.
author: Phys.org

title: Bee Nest Plastic Offers Blueprint for Faster-Degrading Synthetic Plastics
content:
Hundreds of millions of metric tons of plastics are produced each year, and most of them end up in landfills or polluting natural environments after use. These materials can persist for decades to centuries.  

Researchers are actively searching for ways to reduce this environmental burden. A recent study suggests that the answer may lie in nature.  

Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the study shows that a natural plastic produced by bees could provide design insights for creating plastics that degrade in soil much more quickly.
summary: A study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences shows that a natural plastic made by bees could guide the design of plastics that break down more quickly in soil. The research suggests that bee nest materials offer lessons for creating synthetic plastics that degrade naturally in far less time.
author: Phys.org

title: US Wildfire Damage Expected to Triple by Midcentury, Study Finds
content: A new study, published by the author and colleagues, shows that rising temperatures and expanding development are projected to triple the number of homes and other structures damaged or destroyed by wildfires across the United States by mid‑century.
summary: A study just published by the authors shows that rising temperatures and expanding development are increasing the number of homes and other structures damaged or destroyed by wildfires across the U.S. The study predicts that this damage will triple by midcentury.
author: Phys.org

title: Cold without consequences? Short-term climate fluctuations appear to have had less impact on early farmers
content:
A new study from the Leibniz‑Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA) in Germany, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, argues that cold conditions were unlikely to have caused the centuries‑long pause in the spread of farming across south‑eastern Europe during prehistory.  

The research examined the Greek archaeological site of Franchthi and found no evidence of extreme cold there. In addition, the study reported no statistically significant link between local temperature fluctuations and changes in how people obtained their food.
summary: Cold without consequences? Short-term climate fluctuations appear to have had less impact on early farmers.
author: Phys.org

title: Sea‑level rise impacts inland daily life through food, goods, energy, and taxes.
content: Rising sea levels may seem like a distant issue for inland residents, yet they affect daily life. Even far from the coast, sea‑level changes influence the food we eat, the goods we buy, the energy we use, and the taxes we pay.
summary: Rising sea levels can affect the food we eat, the goods we buy, the energy we use, and the taxes we pay. This impact occurs even miles from the coast for people living inland.
author: Phys.org

title: Pregnant mandrill monkeys are more likely to miscarry when also nursing an infant
content: A study published in PLOS Biology reports that female mandrills are more likely to experience pregnancy loss when they are simultaneously nursing an infant. The researchers suggest this may indicate a physiological trade‑off between caring for a current offspring and supporting a future pregnancy. The study was conducted by Nikolaos Smit of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Germany, the University of Turku in Finland, and colleagues.
summary: Pregnant mandrill monkeys are more likely to miscarry when also nursing an infant.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists map Kīlauea's magma reservoirs in high resolution
content: The Hawaiian volcano Kīlauea, one of Earth’s most active volcanoes, experienced near-continuous eruptions from 1983 to 2018 and resumed erupting in late 2024, with activity ongoing through late 2026. This sustained volcanic activity and the site’s accessibility have allowed scientists to gather extensive data for high-resolution mapping of its magma reservoirs.
summary: Scientists are mapping Kīlauea's magma reservoirs in high resolution. The Hawaiian volcano has erupted almost continuously from 1983 to 2018 and began a new series of eruptions in late 2024 that continue as of late 2026, and its activity and accessibility have allowed scientists to collect a wealth of data.
author: Phys.org

title: The nuclear waste repository in Finland designed to outlast modern civilisation
content: Onkalo, a nuclear waste repository in Finland, is set to begin operations. It is described as the first engineered structure designed to last for 100,000 years. The facility is located deep underground and aims to provide a safe storage site for the country’s nuclear waste.
summary: The nuclear waste repository in Finland designed to outlast modern civilisation.
author: New Scientist

title: Study Finds Daily Avocado and Mango Boost Heart Health in Prediabetes
content:
A recent study examined the effects of daily consumption of an avocado and a cup of mango on heart health in adults with pre‑diabetes. Over an eight‑week period, participants showed notable improvements in blood vessel function and a reduction in diastolic blood pressure, with the most pronounced benefits observed in men.

The study found that these cardiovascular gains occurred without any weight gain or changes in overall calorie intake. Researchers suggest that the nutrient‑rich combination of avocado and mango could offer a simple dietary adjustment to support cardiovascular health.
summary: Study with adults with prediabetes found that eating an avocado and a cup of mango daily for eight weeks improved blood vessel function and lowered diastolic blood pressure, especially in men. The improvements happened without weight gain or changes in calorie intake.
author: Science Daily

title: All five DNA/RNA nucleobases found in 4.5‑billion‑year‑old asteroid Ryugu
content: Scientists have identified all five essential nucleobases—adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine, and uracil—present in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu. This discovery shows that the key ingredients for DNA and RNA existed in space billions of years ago. It reinforces evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that such molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
summary: Scientists discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu. The result indicates that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago and were likely widespread throughout the early Solar System.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists link pregnancy inflammation and placental damage to autism traits in male mice
content: Scientists have identified a link between pregnancy inflammation, placental damage, and autism-like traits in male mice, noting that females appeared naturally protected. This discovery may help explain the higher diagnosis rates in boys and offer new opportunities for early intervention.
summary: Scientists discovered a connection between inflammation during pregnancy, placental damage, and autism-like traits in male mice. Female mice were naturally protected, and the findings could explain the higher autism diagnosis in boys and suggest early intervention opportunities.
author: Science Daily

title: Brain's Fear Mechanism Blurs Danger-Safety Line, Explaining Anxiety and PTSD
content:
Researchers using augmented reality to observe mouse brain activity have discovered that fear can cause memories of threatening and harmless environments to overlap. This blurring of the line between danger and safety appears to be a survival mechanism designed to allow for faster responses to potential threats.

The study suggests this "better safe than sorry" approach may explain why individuals with anxiety or PTSD experience intense fear in completely safe situations. By merging distinct environmental memories, the brain prioritizes rapid reaction over precise differentiation, potentially leading to misplaced fear responses in humans.
summary: Scientists used augmented reality to observe brain activity in mice and found that memories of threatening and harmless environments overlapped. This overlap may allow faster responses to danger and could explain why people with anxiety or PTSD sometimes experience intense fear in safe situations.
author: Science Daily

title: 50-year-old Brazil frog disappearance mystery solved by fungus evidence
content: Scientists have identified a deadly fungus as the cause of a nearly 50-year-old mystery regarding disappearing frog populations in Brazil. Evidence indicates the pathogen devastated vulnerable species in the region. Subsequently, many of these frog populations have rebounded, suggesting they developed greater tolerance to the disease that previously threatened their survival.
summary: Scientists have found evidence that a deadly fungus caused the disappearance of frogs in Brazil, solving a nearly 50-year-old mystery. Many frog populations have since rebounded, indicating increased tolerance to the disease.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Find Sound Recognition, Vocabulary, and Background Knowledge Key to Reading Success
content:
A massive new study found that intelligence has a surprisingly limited role in children’s reading success, and visual processing shows no meaningful connection.  

The strongest predictors identified were sound recognition, vocabulary, and background knowledge, offering new clues for helping struggling readers.
summary: A massive new study shows that intelligence has a surprisingly limited role in children's reading success. The study finds that sound recognition, vocabulary, and background knowledge are the strongest predictors, while visual processing shows no meaningful connection.
author: Science Daily

title: Voyager 1 to Reach One Light-Day from Earth on Nov. 18
content:
NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, scheduled for November 18. On that date, the spacecraft will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, a point where even the simplest round-trip communication will take 48 hours.

This achievement comes as engineers manage dwindling power and address mysterious technical issues. A recent unexplained 48-hour communications blackout caused concern, but a clever energy-saving maneuver has successfully extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission.
summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth on November 18, marking a historic milestone nearly 50 years after launch. Engineers are dealing with dwindling power and a recent 48‑hour communications blackout, but an energy‑saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission.
author: Science Daily

title: Hera Captures First Clear View of Asteroids from NASA's 2022 Redirection Experiment
content:
Europe’s Hera spacecraft has taken its first clear images of the two asteroids that were part of NASA’s 2022 kinetic‑impact experiment to deflect a potentially hazardous space rock.  

Now heading toward the pair, Hera will study the collision’s aftermath and investigate why the asteroid’s trajectory shifted far more than scientists had predicted.
summary: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of the two asteroids involved in NASA’s 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Hera is now approaching the pair to investigate the collision aftermath and determine why the asteroid shifted more than scientists predicted.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Astronaut Anil Menon to Connect with Students for National STEM Day Call
content:
NASA’s Office of STEM Engagement is hosting a live, interactive call for National STEM Day that will connect students nationwide with a NASA astronaut and a STEM educator. On Wednesday, November 4, the event will begin at 11 a.m. EST and will be streamed on NASA’s flagship YouTube channel and the Learn With NASA channels.

The call will feature Expedition 74 flight engineer Anil Menon aboard the International Space Station. From the ISS’s Quest airlock, Menon will answer student questions about living and working in microgravity, the path to becoming an astronaut, and the technologies that enable human spaceflight. Mark Rober, a STEM content creator and founder of the ClassCrunchLabs Foundation, will join from California to discuss how curiosity, creativity, and hands‑on problem‑solving guided his transition from NASA engineer to STEM educator.

During the downlink, students will see the space station in real time as Menon demonstrates how everyday activities—such as eating and experimenting—change in microgravity. The session is part of NASA’s broader effort to provide authentic STEM experiences that build technical skills and introduce aerospace careers.

This event also marks the launch of a new partnership between NASA and the ClassCrunchLabs Foundation. Together, the organizations will expand access to STEM learning by aligning NASA’s mission‑driven resources with CrunchLabs’ hands‑on engineering content. Educators and families are encouraged to tune in and celebrate National STEM Day with this inspiring conversation. For more information on NASA in‑flight calls, visit https://www.nasa.gov/stemonstation.
summary: NASA Astronaut Anil Menon to Connect with Students for National STEM Day Call.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Chip Resistors Crack During Thermal Cycling After Vibration Testing
content: For more information, contact Joel W. Sills, Langley Research Center, joel. W. Sills@nasa. Gov. Download PDF here Chip resistors are widely used in NASA projects, yet cases of alumina substrate cracking during environmental testing are rare. Two instances of thick-film chip resistor cracking were observed during thermal cycling after vibration, with fractures occurring across the short axis due to bending. Failure analyses ruled out defective lots and fatigue, identifying board flexure, component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses as contributing factors. The bulletin recommends careful component placement, finite element analysis, controlled solder fillet height, thorough inspection, and functional thermal shock testing to mitigate flexure-induced cracking risks in ceramic body components on printed circuit boards. Background The NESC noted historical lack of reported cases of chip resistors’ alumina substrate cracking during vibration and thermal cycling, although chip resistors are ubiquitous across NASA projects. Two instances of thick film chip resistor body cracking were observed during environmental acceptance testing on printed circuit board assemblies. Both failures occurred during thermal cycling after vibration testing, exhibiting intermittent open circuit failures at hot dwell temperatures that recovered at room temperature. Transverse fracture occurred at the mid-span of each resistor, running parallel to the terminations. The two resistors were installed in similar locations near the edge of the boards on two identical boards. Cracks in failed resistors were along the short axis of the resistor due to apparent bending of the resistors, Figure 1. Resistors showed no signs of pre-existing defects. Causal Relationships Initial theories pointed to vibration-induced damage of potentially defective resistors since both resistors came from the same production lot. However, the resistor lot not only meets the requirements of procurement specification MIL-PRF-55342 but additional tests were performed and did not reveal any direct evidence of a defective resistor lot. There was no evidence of an elevated risk of defective resistors within the production lot. Failure Analyses Independent failure analyses concluded that the cracked chip resistors were due to bending/tensile failures. There was no clear-cut root cause or visible defect identifying a crack initiation site. Both resistors exhibited a single, straight crack across the short axis (perpendicular to the long axis), indicating a bending/tensile failure without twisting. The damage signatures are not consistent with cyclic fatigue, likely ruling out fatigue failure during vibration. In addition, NESC independent optical and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Figure 2, of both resistors did not identify any clear flaw locations for fatigue damage initiation and progression; therefore, the possibility of defective resistors as well as fatigue vibration as the root cause becomes unlikely. Cause Conclusions No direct root cause was identified, but contributing factors leading to increased design consideration needed for large footprint ceramic components located near the edges of a printed circuit board that can lead to stress cracks due to manufacturing or installation bow/twist of the printed circuit board include: Location of the relatively large resistors (case size 2512) next to the edge of the board with resistor’s long axis parallel to the card edge, increasing susceptibility to board flexure-induced damage. Excessive solder that extended to the top pads on the resistor terminations. Excessive bending moments or loads resulting from board bow/twist. Hard mounting the board to a rigid frame, which can store and amplify these bow/twist stresses. Suboptimal fastener torquing patterns, which may concentrate mounting stresses specifically at the resistor locations. Guidelines for Assembly of Ceramic Body Components to Printed Circuit Boards The following guidelines are to be considered given the recent experience. Component Orientation: Avoid orienting the long axis of large footprint ceramic components parallel to nearby printed circuit board edges to reduce susceptibility to global and local flexure damage. Finite Element Analysis: Perform sufficient Finite Element Analysis to demonstrate adequate stress and displacement margins on large components when they must be placed near the edge of the board. Solder Joint Fillet Limits: Keep solder off the top surface of terminations. Solder on top creates a rigid joint that transfers printed circuit board flexure directly into the ceramic increasing risk of flexure-induced cracking. Consult the individual parts manufacturers for guidance, as they may place specific limits on solder fillet height. Solder Joint Inspection: Inspect physical solder joints or review photographic images of the joints to verify that components have sufficient, but not excessive, solder fillets according to manufacturer limits. Functional Thermal Shock Testing: Perform one to three thermal cycles, including a hot-dwell functional test, prior to vibration testing, to document as built component integrity. References 1. MIL-PRF-55342 Resistor, Chip, Fixed, Film, Nonestablished Reliability, Established Reliability, Space Level 2. MIL-PRF-55342/9 Resistor, Fixed, Film, Chip, Nonestablished Reliability, Established Reliability, Space Level, Style RM2512 3. MIL-STD-202 Method 218 Board Flex
summary: Two thick‑film chip resistors on identical boards cracked during thermal cycling after vibration, with fractures running across the short axis due to board flexure. Failure analysis ruled out defective lots and fatigue, recommending careful component placement, finite element analysis, controlled solder fillet height, thorough inspection, and functional thermal shock testing to mitigate flexure‑induced cracking.
author: NASA News

title: CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk and NASA’s Anil Menon install new solar array on ISS
content:
Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was photographed during a spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026 as the International Space Station orbited 267 miles above the South Atlantic Ocean. During that EVA, Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon installed a new roll‑out solar array and completed preparatory tasks for a subsequent EVA scheduled for Nov. 5, 2026.

The upcoming EVA will see the pair install the station’s eighth and final roll‑out solar array, bringing the total to eight arrays that can raise the ISS’s available power by up to 30%. Image credit: CSA.
summary: CSA CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk is pictured during the Oct. 29, 2026, spacewalk.
author: NASA News

title: OpenAI silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
content:
A user on Hacker News reported that the data‑sharing setting for OpenAI’s Codex chat had been silently re‑enabled. The user and coworkers, who had previously disabled the “Improve the model for everyone” option to protect intellectual property, noticed the setting had changed without their action. The setting can be checked at https://chatgpt.com/settings/data-controls, and the user notes that the option can also be turned off via https://privacy.openai.com/policies?Modal=take-control.

The issue was flagged earlier on Hacker News (item 49643556) and has since generated a discussion (item 50352757) with 265 points and 84 comments. The post highlights concerns about unintended data sharing in OpenAI’s code‑generation models.
summary: Users discovered that the data sharing setting for Codex chats had been silently reenabled, allowing OpenAI to use the chats to improve the model. The setting can be disabled again through the settings page or the privacy policy link, and the issue has been discussed on YCombinator.
author: Hacker News

title: GitBook Breach: AI-Driven Attack Exposed Credentials and API Tokens
content:
GitBook has disclosed a security incident involving a sophisticated attack that utilized AI agents to gain unauthorized access to the company’s infrastructure. The breach occurred on November 2 at 19:00 CET, when attackers accessed certain infrastructure credentials. GitBook stated that it detected the intrusion immediately and took the GitBook app and authenticated documentation sites offline to secure its systems, while keeping publicly published content live using cached data.

According to the company’s update, the investigation revealed that the attacker may have accessed Git Sync secrets, GitBook API tokens, third-party API tokens used for external tool connections, and questions submitted to the GitBook Assistant by site visitors. GitBook reported no evidence that customer content within the platform was modified during the incident.

To mitigate the impact, GitBook blocked the attacker, closed the relevant vulnerabilities, and replaced all credentials and secrets across its infrastructure. The company also invalidated all customer API tokens on its platform. Services were restored only after GitBook confirmed that its infrastructure was secure, though some services may still experience degraded performance as full restoration continues.

Customers are advised to rotate any existing GitBook API tokens, third-party API tokens, and secrets used in published integrations. Additionally, users of the GitBook MCP server are instructed to re-authenticate. GitBook stated that it is currently monitoring for further attacks, implementing additional security measures, and preparing a full post-mortem report with detailed information about the incident.
summary: GitBook disclosed that attackers used AI agents to access infrastructure credentials on November 2, potentially exposing Git Sync secrets and API tokens. The company has restored services and advised users to rotate affected tokens while reporting no evidence of content modification.
author: Hacker News

title: Reverse Game Theory Aims to Control AI Agents; Trump Rebrands AI as “Super Intelligence”
content: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. While game theory predicts how rational actors behave under particular rules, reverse game theory designs rules to elicit the behavior we want. Think of splitting a cake: if one person cuts it and the other gets first choice, the cutter has an incentive to make the portions equal. Researchers believe the approach could align AI more closely with our rules and instructions. But big questions remain about whether these mechanisms will work in practice. Here’s how reverse game theory could help make AI agents behave. —Amit Katwala Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order with just one directive: government agencies must rebrand artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” One month on, the rebrand is slowly appearing across government websites and documents, but it hasn’t caught on with everyone. Even some of the biggest names in tech still use “AI.” But the bigger concern is the new term becoming a political loyalty test: Those who use it signal allegiance to the administration. Those who don’t become targets for attacks. So one month in, who’s on board? —James O’Donnell This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Today’s midterms will test AI’s influence on US politics Candidates are betting that AI regulation will sway voters to their side. ( FT $) + The move follows pressure from Washington. ( Bloomberg $) + Chinese AI has ruptured the White House. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 Hackers have turned supermarket fridges into a food security risk Attacks in Europe have put US supermarket systems on alert. ( CNBC ) + They’ve also sparked concerns over other domestic appliances. ( BBC ) + It’s a good time for doing crime. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 Scientists have detected signals at the smallest scale ever explored The discovery offers clues to a world of exotic new particles. ( BBC ) + It came via CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. ( The Times $) 5 Zapping part of the brain makes you think harder—at a cost It can both improve performance and reduce motivation. ( New Scientist $) + Neuropixels probes are transforming how we study the brain. ( Nature ) 6 Big tech is splurging on mega gas plants to power data centers The projectsthreaten to reverse years of climate pledges. ( WP $) 7 Google says an Android partner infected 1.3 million devices The malware infected TV boxes and other Android-based devices. ( Verge ) 8 Apple is trying to create its first robot It’s proving a lot harder than expected, though. ( Information $) + AI robots are still a long way from useful. ( MIT Technology Review ) 9 China’s biggest shopping festival has a new product to sell: AI AI tokens have become a major new Singles’ Day category. ( Reuters $) 10 A meteorite in the Sahara has revealed new clues about Mars Its chemistry may help explain how the planet lost its water. ( Wired $) Quote of the day “Don’t spend money unduly by asking a human expert to enter into a debate with a robot expert.” —Steven Benmor, a family lawyer, tells the Wall Street Journal that clients increasingly need to pay human experts to correct advice they’ve received from chatbots. One more thing The noise we make is hurting animals. Can we learn to shut up? As human society has expanded, animals have started struggling to hear one another. For many birds, the noise has grown so loud that they’ve begun to sing with faster trills. Now, their mating calls aren’t as effective. The growing hubbub can also increase bird-on-bird conflict, and entire species that can’t handle urban clamor simply leave town for good. But there are technological solutions to the noises hurting animals—and they could help humans, too. —Clive Thompson We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. summary: Researchers propose reverse game theory to design rules that incentivize powerful AI models to follow desired behavior. President Trump signed an executive order rebranding artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence”, a move that is becoming a political loyalty test among government agencies and tech companies.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Binance Reports $6.34B Hack by North Korean Attackers Using Fake Interview
content: Binance reported that a suspected North Korean hacking group carried out a $6.34 billion theft from its systems. The attackers deceived an engineer with a fake job interview and a malicious download, which allowed them to gain a foothold and steal billions, according to the company.
summary: Suspected North Korean attackers duped a Binance engineer with a fake job interview and a malicious download. The intrusion gave them a foothold in Binance’s system and allowed them to steal billions, according to Binance.
author: Wired

title: Xbox Nano Controller to Connect Directly to Cloud Gaming Over Wi-Fi
content:
Microsoft will release its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow.  The device contains a hidden feature that lets it connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi‑Fi, a capability that has not yet been officially announced.

The direct‑cloud connection is intended to reduce latency, mirroring the approach used by Google’s Stadia controllers.  Microsoft is privately testing the feature on the new Xbox Cloud Gaming website, and it will require users to pair the Nano controller over Wi‑Fi with Microsoft’s cloud servers.
summary: Microsoft is about to launch its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow. The Nano can connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi-Fi to improve latency, a feature still privately tested.
author: The Verge

title: Moft Unveils Dynamic Folio Case for iPhone Duo with Kickstand and Grip
content:
Moft has re‑engineered its Dynamic Folio, originally launched in early 2025 for the iPad, into a new case for Apple’s iPhone Duo. The updated design adds a kickstand that lets the Duo rest at multiple angles for hands‑free use, and its origami‑style screen cover can double as a finger grip while holding the phone.  

The Dynamic Folio Case for iPhone Duo is available for preorder on Moft’s online store at $89.99. Buyers can choose navy blue, misty cove, or sapphire. Shipping is slated to begin in mid‑December, and the price represents a modest increase over Moft’s earlier offering.
summary: Moft has redesigned its Dynamic Folio as a case for the iPhone Duo that can be used as a kickstand and finger grip. The case is available for preorder at $89.99 in navy blue, misty cove, and sapphire, with shipping expected to start in mid December.
author: The Verge

title: Netflix Adds AI Discover Tab to Show Theme‑Based Recommendations
content:
Netflix is introducing a new "AI Discover" tab to its TV app, featuring experimental, AI-powered tools designed to assist users in finding new content. The initial experiment presents thematic categories such as "Something Light," "Family Movie Night," and "Quick Watches." Selecting a theme generates corresponding show and movie recommendations tailored to that specific mood or occasion.

The platform allows users to provide feedback on these suggestions, with the app retaining negative responses to refine future picks. Netflix states that AI Discover operates on a new intelligence layer built to respond to member input in real time while continuously learning from user interactions.
summary: Netflix’s TV app will feature a new “AI Discover” tab that surfaces experimental, AI‑powered recommendations. The tab offers theme‑based suggestions such as “Something Light” and “Family Movie Night,” and learns from user feedback in real time.
author: The Verge

title: Google Home Speaker with Gemini AI drops to $79, 20% off at major retailers
content:
Google’s newest Home Speaker, powered by the Gemini AI model, is now being offered at a discount of roughly 20 percent. The device, which launched in June, is listed for $79—down from its regular $99.99 price—at major retailers including Best Buy, Walmart and Target, and is available in four color options.

The speaker’s design has been highlighted for its compact size, which is smaller than the previous‑generation Nest Audio, making it easy to place in various rooms. Reviewers noted that despite its reduced footprint the unit delivers loud, clear 360‑degree audio, and in comparative testing it sounded cleaner and sharper than the similarly priced Amazon Echo Dot Max, though some reviewers preferred the Echo’s fuller bass. The older Nest Audio is still regarded as having superior overall sound, but the new model offers a lower price and smaller size.

In addition to audio performance, the Google Home Speaker supports the Matter standard and includes a Thread border router, enabling control of a broad range of compatible smart‑home devices. It can also serve as an audio output for the Google TV Streamer 4K, allowing TV sound to be played through one or two speakers instead of the TV’s built‑in speakers.

A key feature of the device is its Gemini‑based assistant, which is described as more adept at natural‑language and complex requests than the earlier Google Assistant. Reviewers observed that Gemini can handle multiple smart‑home commands simultaneously and respond to conversational prompts, such as adjusting the air conditioner when a temperature complaint is mentioned. Some Gemini capabilities, including “Gemini Live” for extended conversations without repeating the wake word, require a $10‑per‑month Google Home Premium subscription.
summary: We’re big fans of the Google Home Speaker’s design. | Photo: Jennifer Patison Tuohy / The Verge If you’re looking for a good smart speaker, the Google Home Speaker is down to around $79 ($20 off) in all four colors at Best Buy, Walmart, and Target.
author: The Verge

title: Steam approval delays cause indie game Food Devils to miss planned launch
content:
Indie developers are reporting that Steam’s approval process is causing unexpected delays, leading some games to miss their scheduled launch dates. A screenshot of the upcoming title Food Devils shows the game listed as missing its planned release today. The developer, Studio Daimon, submitted the game’s build to Steam on October 12 and intended to launch in early access on the same day.

According to a post by game director Alfred Kamon, the build is “still awaiting approval,” and the team does not know when Steam will grant final clearance. Kamon noted that the studio sent an additional support ticket last week to inquire about the situation. Other indie developers have similarly posted on social media about unusually long wait times for Steam’s game‑submission approvals.
summary: Indie developers have posted about unusually long Steam approval wait times that are causing missed launch dates. Studio Daimon's title Food Devils, submitted on October 12, remained awaiting approval on its scheduled early‑access launch day, with director Alfred Kamon saying Steam has not yet given final OK.
author: The Verge

title: Reddit tests ads in search results
content:
Reddit is expanding its advertising program by testing ads in the platform’s search results. The company says the ads will be placed “based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a search query,” so a query such as “espresso station” could show ads for espresso products, while “home office setup” might display ads for monitors, desks or chairs.  

Reddit already serves ads across its feeds in formats that include images, videos, sponsored posts, AMAs and within discussion threads. The new search‑based placement is part of a broader set of platform changes announced by Reddit.
summary: Reddit is testing ads that appear within its search results based on factors such as contextual relevance to a query. The platform already shows ads across feeds, threads and in formats including images, videos, sponsored posts and AMAs.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI says ChatGPT queries now equal 20% of Google searches
content:
OpenAI announced that the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. The statement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.  

Fry explained that OpenAI defines a “search” as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, distinguishing it from tasks such as defining a term or providing a simple how‑to explanation.  

He did not disclose the source of the Google search‑volume figure. Despite matching one‑fifth of Google’s search traffic, OpenAI noted that this level is still a long way from overtaking the search‑engine giant.
summary: OpenAI announced that the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. The announcement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.
author: The Verge

title: Apple watchOS 27.3 beta adds always‑on Audio Intelligence with Siri Recap and Live Rewind
content:
Apple has begun rolling out the watchOS 27.3 developer beta, which adds always‑on Audio Intelligence capabilities to the Apple Watch. The update enables Siri to access the watch’s microphone and introduces two features: Siri Recap, which uses ambient listening to create conversation summaries, and Live Rewind, which provides text transcripts of the most recent 15 seconds of detected audio.

In the same release, Apple is making a redesigned Health app available for testing in the iOS 27.3 developer beta and has announced expanded language support that includes global English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish and Turkish.
summary: Apple watchOS 27.3 beta adds always‑on Audio Intelligence with Siri Recap and Live Rewind.
author: The Verge

title: Mercedes-Benz develops holographic heads-up display for car interiors
content:
Mercedes‑Benz arranged for a representative from Ars to travel from Los Angeles to Stuttgart, Germany, and provided accommodation so the outlet could experience the company’s new holographic display. The article notes that Ars does not accept paid editorial content.

The piece places the holographic display in the context of an increasing number of screens in luxury car interiors, describing how screens have grown larger, multiplied across dashboards and taken on new forms. It questions whether consumers actually desire more screens and observes that premium features eventually filter down to mainstream vehicles, limiting how large screens can become.

Mercedes‑Benz’s holographic display is presented as a next‑step alternative to traditional screens. Described as a more advanced form of heads‑up display (HUD), it aims to move beyond conventional visual interfaces without invoking science‑fiction imagery. The article invites readers to view the full story for additional details.
summary: Mercedes-Benz is working on a new holographic display, described as a more advanced form of heads-up display. The company provided flights from Los Angeles to Stuttgart, Germany, and accommodation so Ars could experience the technology.
author: Ars Technica

title: EPA ends 20-year effort to monitor factory farm air pollution
content:
The Environmental Protection Agency announced late last week that it will end a more‑than‑20‑year effort to develop methods for monitoring air pollution from factory farms. The agency said the decision effectively halts its attempts to regulate these facilities under the Clean Air Act.

The announcement, made just days before the midterm elections, was described by the EPA as a long‑awaited reprieve for farmers, a constituency the agency noted as historically important to former President Trump and the Republican Party.

Factory farms house tens of thousands of animals in confined spaces, and the agency’s statement noted that waste can be released through ventilation fans or from large lagoons of liquid effluent. Such livestock operations emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide and volatile organic compounds, a mix the agency said contributes to air pollution. Research cited in the release linked emissions from these operations to nearly 12,700 deaths annually in the United States.
summary: EPA ends 20-year effort to monitor factory farm air pollution.
author: Ars Technica

title: Meta temporarily suspends No Kings Instagram account during early voting push
content:
Over the weekend, the No Kings Coalition reported that Meta declined to commit to measures that would prevent automated systems from suspending one of Instagram’s most prominent pro‑democracy accounts if activity around the page surged during the midterm elections. The coalition’s demand followed Meta’s apology for temporarily suspending the No Kings Instagram account and disabling access for four hours during a peak period of an early‑voting push by the group.

In a post on X, Meta’s Andy Stone explained that the account had been using a Claude AI tool in a manner that made it appear to be a bot. Stone said automated review detected the error within an hour, but additional hurdles kept administrators locked out of the account. State and federal lawmakers, as well as a coalition of 14 attorneys general, have asked Meta to provide a fuller explanation of its actions.

Meta responded by offering a meeting with a technical expert to clarify the mistake, but the No Kings Coalition rejected that proposal. The group requested a meeting with Meta senior leadership instead, arguing that the issue extends beyond its Instagram account and that Americans need assurance that voting content will not be suppressed ahead of or on election day. Among eight questions, the coalition asked Meta to publicly disclose any communications with the Trump administration regarding the No Kings account or the historic early‑voting day event.
summary: Meta apologized after temporarily suspending the No Kings Instagram account and disabling access for four hours during an early‑voting push. The No Kings Coalition rejected Meta’s offer of a technical‑expert meeting, demanding senior leadership talks and disclosure of any communications with the Trump administration, while lawmakers and 14 attorneys general have asked for further explanation.
author: Ars Technica

title: UEFI bootkit BlackLotus infects fully patched Windows 11 systems
content:
In 2023 researchers documented a malware family called BlackLotus, the first publicly observed UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. By subverting the industry‑wide chain‑of‑trust mechanism, the bootkit was able to execute malicious code before the operating system and its security defenses were fully loaded.

Microsoft had already released a patch for the vulnerability exploited by BlackLotus in 2022. Subsequent updates in 2023 and 2024 added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers and introduced a method to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers.

Despite these mitigations, a later variant tracked as BlackX infected organizations that had applied all of the aforementioned patches. The article notes that the infected systems had the full set of updates, prompting questions about how the bootkit succeeded despite the existing protections. A brief overview of UEFI’s role in initializing hardware and loading the OS is also provided.
summary: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in‑the‑wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 computers. The organizations infected by the newer bootkit, tracked as BlackX, had installed Microsoft’s 2022 patch and the 2023‑2024 updates that added a new certificate and revocation capability.
author: Ars Technica

title: Argo Space bets its future on water propulsion for in‑space travel
content:
Three engineers who spent the Falcon 9 era at SpaceX—Robert, Ryan and Kirby Carlisle—have left the company to pursue a new venture in space. After working on launching, refurbishing and selling rockets, the brothers decided to focus on spacecraft rather than rockets when they founded their own firm.

In late 2022 the Carlisle brothers established Argo Space, a company aimed at building infrastructure in orbit. Their stated goal is to enable in‑space transportation without relying on propellants launched from Earth. To that end, Argo Space has selected water as its propulsion medium, citing its potential to be harvested on the Moon and its abundance throughout the Solar System.
summary: The Carlisle brothers—Robert, Ryan and Kirby—who worked at SpaceX during the Falcon 9 era founded Argo Space in late 2022 to build space infrastructure. The company plans to use water, harvestable on the Moon and abundant throughout the Solar System, as a propellant to eliminate the need for Earth‑sourced fuel.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google shuts down x. Cpe botnet affecting 1.3 million Android TV boxes
content:
Google’s Threat Intelligence Group announced that it has dismantled a large botnet known as x. Cpe.  The network operated on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices that had been certified by Google, and it was traced to boxes manufactured by Shenzhen‑based Videostrong Technology.  According to the group’s blog post, the malware used obfuscation techniques that allowed it to bypass Google’s certification screening.

The compromised devices, most of which were sold under the MECOOL brand, contained a backdoor that let the attacker install the botnet after the boxes were set up and connected online.  A stub application identified as x. Cpe or com. Oemservice phoned home, held system‑level permissions, and could install additional malware modules while disabling Play Protect, which would otherwise flag the packages as malicious.  The botnet evolved from a single‑stage dropper into a modular three‑stage platform that offered access to third parties.
summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group says it has shut down a massive botnet called x. Cpe.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google lets schools disable AI tools, but they lose access to Search
content: Google is offering schools the option to turn off its AI tools. However, the company notes that schools that choose to block AI entirely will also lose access to Google Search, because AI features are now built into the search engine.
summary: Google will let schools disable its AI tools. Schools that restrict AI will no longer be able to use Google Search because AI features are now integrated into the search engine.
author: TechCrunch

title: Binance fights brand damage after record $6.3bn crypto hack
content:
The world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance, is confronting a wave of angry customers after a record‑breaking hack that cost roughly $6.3 billion. The incident has sparked a brand‑recovery effort as the platform seeks to manage the fallout and restore user confidence.

The discussion of the hack appears in TechScape, a newsletter that examines how technology shapes daily life. The current issue highlights the Binance breach alongside other tech‑related topics, and invites readers to share whether they have been affected by the incident.
summary: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, is facing fallout from a record $6.3 billion hack and angry customers. The company is working to protect its brand after the breach.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Qatar sees hope for US-Iran interim deal despite fresh US strikes
content: Qatar said on Tuesday that it sees hope for an interim U.S.–Iran agreement as mediators continue to exchange proposals in real time. The statement noted that fresh U.S. strikes and ongoing threats to shipping through the Hormuz Strait are complicating efforts to end the Iran war.
summary: Qatar said Tuesday it saw hope for an interim deal as mediators continue to exchange proposals. Fresh US strikes and threats to shipping through Hormuz continue to complicate efforts to end the Iran war.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea and Turkey sign financing pact to fund nuclear projects, including Sinop plant
content: Turkey and South Korea have signed a financing agreement that explores funding for nuclear projects, reflecting an expansion of nuclear, defence and trade ties between the two nations. Ankara is weighing potential partners for its planned Sinop nuclear power plant, with Seoul seeking a role in the project.
summary: Turkey and South Korea are expanding nuclear, defence and trade ties. Their latest agreement explores funding for nuclear projects, while Ankara weighs potential partners for its planned Sinop plant.
author: Euronews

title: Americans vote in midterms that will decide Congress control for Trump's final two years
content: Voters are casting ballots in Fairfax, Virginia, and in New York as Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections. These elections will decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.
summary: Voters cast ballots in Fairfax, Virginia, and New York. The midterm elections will determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term.
author: Euronews

title: Senate races in unexpected Republican states will decide midterm control
content: Democrats appear poised to secure the U.S. House, while control of the Senate hinges on a few competitive races in states that Republicans had not anticipated needing to defend. Those contests will determine which party holds the Senate after the midterm elections.
summary: Democrats look all but certain to take the US House. The real fight is for the Senate, where a handful of races in states Republicans never expected to defend will decide who controls Washington.
author: Euronews

title: James Talarico leads polls in Texas Senate race aiming to end Democrats' 30-year streak
content: Democratic candidate James Talarico is currently leading the polls in Texas ahead of the U.S. Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is among the most closely watched midterm battles, as Democrats aim to end a 30‑year losing streak in the state. The story is reported by Andrés Espinal from Austin, Texas.
summary: In Texas, Democratic candidate James Talarico is leading the polls ahead of a high-stakes US Senate race against Republican Ken Paxton. The contest is one of the most closely watched battles of the midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to end a 30-year losing streak in the state.
author: France 24

title: US Midterm Elections: Over 58 Million Americans Cast Early Ballots
content:
Over 58 million Americans have already cast early ballots for the U.S. midterm elections, a figure that underscores the high level of voter participation ahead of the vote.  

Pollsters have framed the election as a referendum on President Donald Trump, with polls opening in dozens of states to gauge his influence. The prevailing sentiment in those polls is that Democrats are poised to regain the House of Representatives.  

However, the same polls raise the question of whether Democrats could also capture the Senate, potentially blocking Trump’s agenda during his final two years in office.
summary: Polls have opened in dozens of states as a referendum on US President Donald Trump, with most suggesting Democrats will retake the House of Representatives. The Senate outcome could stymie Trump's agenda in his final two years in office.

title: Ukraine's Operation Veles sends troops into disused pipeline in Kupiansk

title: France's dermatologist shortage deepens as half near retirement, only 100 trained yearly
content:
Around 200,000 cases of skin cancer are diagnosed in France every year, yet the country is facing a growing difficulty in securing dermatology appointments. Half of France’s dermatologists are nearing retirement, and only about 100 new specialists are trained each year, creating a widening gap between demand and supply.

The shortage has prompted some professionals to devise innovative solutions to address the crisis. According to a report by FRANCE 24’s Aurore Dupuis and Sonia Baritello, these new approaches aim to improve access to dermatological care amid the mounting shortage.

title: Philippe Jaenada wins Prix Goncourt for true‑crime novel on 1949 Paris murder
content:
Philippe Jaenada was announced on Tuesday afternoon as the winner of France’s most prestigious literary prize, the Prix Goncourt. The award was given for his novel L’Inconnue du quai de Javel (The Unknown Woman of the Quai de Javel).

The novel is a true‑crime investigation that attempts to solve a 77‑year‑old cold case. It focuses on the murder of a 29‑year‑old Breton woman named Louise Cansot, who was a Paris life model in 1949.

Jaenada’s book seeks not only to uncover the facts of the 1949 murder but also to rehabilitate the reputation of its victim, Louise Cansot, bringing new attention to a case long forgotten.
summary: Philippe Jaenada was announced on Tuesday afternoon as the winner of the Prix Goncourt for his novel L’Inconnue du quai de Javel. The book recreates the 1949 murder of 29‑year‑old Breton life model Louise Cansot and seeks to rehabilitate her reputation.

title: Brazil releases first global roadmap to phase out coal, oil and gas
content:
Brazil has released the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels, announcing the plan on Tuesday. The initiative comes from Brazil’s government, which is the host of last year’s UN climate conference and the upcoming COP30 summit.

The roadmap sets out steps to break the link between countries and coal, oil, and gas. It states that nations can begin reducing their fossil‑fuel dependence immediately, without waiting for new technologies or economic shifts. The plan also argues that doing so could boost economies and help lift people out of poverty while moving the focus from negotiating to implementing climate action.
summary: Brazil’s government announced the world’s first global roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday. It says countries can break the link with coal, oil and gas now and could boost economies and pull people out of poverty.

title: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons lead Bears past Seahawks 34-17
content:
The Chicago Bears defeated the host Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night, powered by an efficient performance from quarterback Caleb Williams and a strong defensive showing by new arrival Jeffery Simmons. Williams completed 71% of his passes for 247 yards without turnovers, throwing a touchdown pass on the opening drive. He was sacked only once against one of the NFL’s stingiest defenses.

On defense, Simmons recorded one sack and six tackles. Running back D’Andre Swift added three rushing touchdowns for the Bears, who improved to a 6-2 record. The Seattle Seahawks have lost three of their last four games.
summary: Caleb Williams threw for 247 yards without turnovers while Jeffery Simmons recorded a sack and six tackles as the Bears defeated the Seahawks 34-17. D'Andre Swift rushed for three touchdowns in the victory over a Seattle team that has lost three of its last four games.

title: Denzel Bentley Stripped of WBO Title Over Mandatory Challenge Dispute
content:
Middleweight boxer Denzel Bentley has been stripped of his WBO world title after the sanctioning body refused permission for him to defend his belt against Shane Mosley Jr. The WBO rejected Bentley’s appeal last Friday, which argued he was entitled to face the world-ranked Mosley Jr rather than his mandatory challenger in a first title defence. The decision prevents the fight scheduled for this Saturday night at London’s Copper Box Arena.

In an interview at his gym in Essex, Bentley discussed the trauma and street violence that have impacted his life. He revealed that several friends in Battersea were murdered, an experience that numbed him and placed the current boxing politics into perspective. Bentley described his past reluctance to share his story, noting that he has been chased and shot at. Despite the loss of his title and the surrounding political disputes, he remains determined to continue pursuing fights and titles.
summary: Denzel Bentley has been stripped of his WBO world middleweight title after the sanctioning body refused permission for him to defend against Shane Mosley Jr. Bentley stated that he was entitled to face the world-ranked Mosley Jr rather than his mandatory challenger in a first title defence.

The result marked a significant achievement for trainer Ciaron Maher, who filled the top three places in the event. Point of Law justified his status as the favorite, securing the win in a thrilling finish against his stablemate.

title: Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
content: Forward had cardiac arrest and was taken to hospital He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball The Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel has died following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in Spain’s second division. Tenerife announced that the 30-year-old had tragically passed away at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. De Miguel suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest and did not regain consciousness. The collision occurred in added time at the end of Andorra’s visit to Tenerife, a game that had been put back 24 hours because of the risk of torrential rain on the island. With the score 2-2, late in the 96th minute, a long ball was played away from the Tenerife area and up the pitch. De Miguel chased it into space and Owono came a long way out of his goal, jumping forward and crashing into the attacking player inside the centre circle. Owono was immediately sent off. De Miguel was left unconscious with players from both sides appealing for medical assistance.
summary: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died at age 30 after suffering a cardiac arrest following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono. The incident occurred during a match in Spain’s second division, where Owono was sent off after crashing into De Miguel in the 96th minute.

title: Canada, EU Agree Deeper Cooperation on Energy and Cleantech Supply Chains
content: Canada and the European Union’s commitment to strengthen cooperation on energy security and the energy transition lays the foundation to put clean growth and climate priorities at the heart of their alliance, according to experts. In a seven-page joint statement agreed at the end of a two-day summit in Montreal on Friday, both sides committed to work more closely on investment in critical minerals, green grids, energy sources, battery storage and the protection of energy infrastructure. They agreed to assess opportunities for long-term energy connectivity across the Atlantic, including through a feasibility study on liquefied gas (LNG) exports to Europe. The statement also includes a pledge to “deepen targeted industrial cooperation” on technology value chains and “address bilateral trade barriers”. “Canada and the European Union have sent a clear and unwavering signal that closer cooperation on decarbonisation and climate resilience will be central to their new strategic alliance,” said Canadian Climate Institute president Rick Smith. “The task now is to turn talk into action.” Foundation for climate action The EU and Canada’s “alliance for the future” aims to deepen their partnership across investment, trade and economic security to weather geopolitical tensions and global threats, including “the existential threat of the interdependent crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, ocean and land degradation, and pollution”. These threats are “increasingly impossible to ignore as the impacts of extreme heat, wildfires, floods, and other disasters become more disruptive and expensive,” Smith said. Investment in critical minerals During the summit, the European Investment Bank (EIB) announced a “new chapter” for its presence in Canada, beginning with accelerated investment in critical minerals. “At a time when both sides of the Atlantic are working to reduce strategic dependencies, we want to turn our partnership into investment in real projects, from mining and processing to recycling,” EIB Vice-President Nicolas Beer said in a statement. “That is how we build supply chains that are not only more secure, but more competitive too.” Joanna Kyriazis, director of policy and strategy at Clean Energy Canada, welcomed the EIB announcement as a “bright spot of the summit” and “one of the few tangible actions”. “As the EU and Canada seek to advance a partnership anchored in ensuring mutual security and navigating an uncertain world, it is essential that electrification remains a north star… one of the greatest ways we can advance both short- and long-term affordability, competitiveness, and energy security,” she said. Feasibility of Canadian LNG exports to the EU In addition, the agreement calls for a joint long-term feasibility study on LNG exports to Europe, although no immediate investment was announced to support this. A media briefing circulated by climate advocacy groups in advance of the summit had warned that a call for such a study would support Canada’s efforts to rebrand gas, a highly polluting fossil fuel, as a reliable, low-carbon energy source. Yet, the agreement was interpreted by some observers as a Canadian concession following more than a year of rhetoric predicting a boom in Canadian gas exports to the EU and elsewhere. Yet Koç Holding has become a top partner while its oil refiner runs flat out and its climate targets slip “What is clear is that the EU is reducing its gas consumption drastically,” Adrian Hiel, director of the Brussels-based Electrification Alliance, told the Globe and Mail. “The long-term trend is clear and by the middle of the next decade, Europe should be out of the LNG game.” Last year, The Energy Mix and Berlin-based Clean Energy Wire reported on mounting doubts that serious European demand for additional gas supplies would ever materialise after Energy and Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson touted LNG exports to Germany in “as little as five years”. Rapprochement on a ‘trade irritant’ In the lead-up to the summit, the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation reported that Canadian iron, steel, fertiliser and aluminium would not be exempt from carbon tariffs under the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), as it moves toward full implementation in 2034. The CBAM is a trade tool designed to protect the continent’s domestic industries from competitors in countries with less stringent carbon controls. Unlike other non-EU members like Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and the UK, Canada is unlikely to be exempted from the CBAM because there are no plans to link its carbon market to Europe’s. However, at the end of the Montreal summit, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told a press conference they had made progress on finding joint solutions to the issue, which von der Leyen described as a “trade irritant”. Canada’s EU ambassador, Jonathan Wilkinson, formerly the environment and climate minister, said Canada sees it as a problem that the CBAM “did not acknowledge Canadian producers were doing their part to reduce their greenhouse gas footprint by paying an industrial carbon price”. He “confirmed diplomatic talks are heading in the right direction but not resolved”, CBC reported. A longer version of this story was originally published by The Energy Mix as part of its partnership with Small Change Fund. The post Canada, EU agree deeper cooperation on energy and cleantech supply chains appeared first on Climate Home News.
summary: Canada, EU Agree Deeper Cooperation on Energy and Cleantech Supply Chains.

title: Stony Brook Study Finds AI Improves Efficiency and Accuracy of Discharge Summaries
content: A Stony Brook University study published online in npj Digital Medicine concludes that artificial intelligence could help physicians prepare hospital patient discharge summaries more efficiently and with greater accuracy and completeness. The research suggests AI tools may streamline the creation of these summaries and improve their quality.
summary: A Stony Brook University study concluded that AI can help physicians prepare hospital patient discharge summaries more efficiently and with greater accuracy and completeness. The study was published online in npj Digital Medicine.
